title: A finite-net Gaussian oracle predicts the known orbit without latent identifiability

oracle.channel: In real selected-mode coordinates X=m_Z+xi with Z=(Theta,Y) in T^4, xi Gaussian with uniformly nondegenerate S_0, and known coefficients sqrt(rho_k)c_k.
oracle.lipschitz_bound: For rho_k<=rho_+, d_N=Theta(N^3) and |k|=O(N), squared whitened mean distance is at most C[N^3|Delta Theta|^2+N^5|Delta Y|^2].
oracle.net: Phase mesh N^(-2) and three translation meshes N^(-3) give at most C N^11 means and squared approximation error O(N^(-1)).
oracle.finite_model_risk: Whitened least squares over the finite net and the Gaussian finite-model oracle inequality give expected mean-prediction loss O(log N).
oracle.posterior_transfer: The posterior mean minimizes Bayes quadratic prediction risk, so E Tr[S_0^(-1)Cov(m_Z|X)]=O(log N).
oracle.scope_guard: The theorem predicts the orbit mean and does not uniquely recover latent parameters; aliases and stabilizers are allowed, but unknown coefficients, growing latent dimension and non-orbit laws are not covered.
